resources.name: attorneys
resources.title: Attorneys by county in Ohio, California, Michigan, Idaho, Arizona, Washington and Pennsylvania, from each bar's public counts
resources.description: How many lawyers each bar counts in each county, for seven states. Ohio: attorneys by county of address and status, from the Supreme Court of Ohio's attorney directory list (88 counties, with admission decade, private practice and Spanish speakers). California: active, inactive, judge and not-eligible licensees in each of the 58 counties, from the State Bar's county table. Michigan: active State Bar members living in each of the 83 counties, with private practice and the change from 2024. Idaho: members by status in each of the seven judicial districts. Arizona: active State Bar members in each of the 15 counties (the Bar's 2022 report). Washington: WSBA licensees of every type (lawyers plus limited licensees) in each of the 39 counties, with the attorney counts by member type. Pennsylvania: active attorneys in the seven counties the Disciplinary Board's annual report lists, and the Board's statewide status counts. Each record carries the source's own as-of date and a rate per 10,000 residents from the Census Bureau's county estimate. Only counts are published, and where a count is built from a directory file no name, birthdate, address or registration number is kept or written. In Ohio, counts of one to four in a disciplinary, deceased or other status, an admission decade, private practice or Spanish are withheld, and where a withheld count could be worked out from a county's total or the statewide figures, another count in the same group is withheld too. Every state record ties to its source's own total, and every published number is read a second time from the source file before release.

resources.description: How many cases are filed in state trial courts, by county, court level and case group, from each state court system's own published statistics. Texas (Office of Court Administration): district, constitutional county and statutory county courts, fiscal years 2023–24 and 2024–25, with district-court filings by case type. Washington (Administrative Office of the Courts): superior courts (criminal, civil, domestic, probate, adoption and parentage, mental illness, juvenile dependency and offender) and district and municipal courts (traffic infractions, DUI, other traffic and non-traffic misdemeanors, civil protection orders, civil and small claims), calendar year 2025. Maryland (Judiciary data dashboard): circuit-court filings by case type (tort, contract, divorce, paternity, juvenile, felony and more) and District Court filings (landlord-tenant, civil, criminal, DUI, traffic citations, peace orders and domestic violence), fiscal years 2012 to 2025. Indiana (Office of Judicial Administration): circuit and superior court new filings by Rule 8 case type (felony, misdemeanor, tort, collection, small claims, eviction, foreclosure, domestic relations, estates, guardianship, juvenile), calendar year 2025 (provisional) beside 2024. Wisconsin (Director of State Courts Office): circuit-court cases opened by county and category (felony, misdemeanor, criminal traffic, traffic, civil, small claims, divorce, other family, paternity, adoption, estates and informal probate, guardianship, commitments, juvenile delinquency and child-welfare), 2020 to 2025. Virginia (Supreme Court of Virginia, Office of the Executive Secretary): circuit courts (domestic and family, felony, misdemeanor, general civil, probate, protective orders), general district courts (landlord-tenant, garnishment, civil, felony, misdemeanor, infractions, protective orders) and juvenile and domestic relations district courts (custody and visitation, child support, delinquency, child dependency, protective orders) by locality (county or independent city), calendar year 2025. Pennsylvania (Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts): courts of common pleas in all 67 counties, civil cases by case type (motor-vehicle and other torts, mass torts, medical malpractice, contract and debt collection, landlord-tenant, mortgage foreclosure) and new criminal, protection from abuse, spousal and child support, custody, divorce, juvenile dependency and delinquency, adoption and guardianship cases, calendar year 2024. Oregon (Oregon Judicial Department): circuit courts in all 36 counties (general civil, landlord-tenant, small claims, felony, misdemeanor, violations, divorce, other domestic relations, protective orders, juvenile, probate, civil commitment), calendar year 2025. West Virginia (Supreme Court of Appeals): circuit courts (general civil, felony, misdemeanor, adoption, guardianship, mental health, juvenile), family courts (divorce, domestic violence, other domestic relations) and magistrate courts (small claims, personal safety and domestic violence protective orders) in all 55 counties, calendar year 2025. Every record keeps the state's own category names and the numbers added into each group (components), and carries a harmonized group and the practice areas it bears on, so a county's filings can be read as demand for personal injury, family, landlord-tenant, small claims and debt, probate, criminal and DUI, juvenile and traffic work. In every source the counties add up to the state's own printed total where it prints one (Texas, Washington, Indiana, Wisconsin, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Oregon, West Virginia), and the state rows for Maryland are the sum of the counties because the file prints no statewide row. One record per county or county equivalent (3,223), per state, DC, Puerto Rico and Guam, for foreign countries, the Freely Associated States, other U.S. territories and unknown addresses, and for the US (187,660,338,257 dollars in all). Counties carry the Census FIPS code; Connecticut's counties are the planning regions.

resources.name: vehicle-complaints
resources.title: Vehicle safety complaints by state, make and model year (NHTSA complaint file)
resources.description: Safety complaints about cars, trucks, SUVs, motorcycles and RVs that owners filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), counted from its Office of Defects Investigation complaint file for the ten most recent model years, by the complainant's state, the make, the model year and the part of the vehicle named (engine, brakes, air bags, steering and the other NHTSA component groups). Each record gives the complaints, how many report a crash, a fire, an injury or a death, the people reported injured and killed, the complaints filed in the last twelve months, and how many concern a make, model and year that has a safety recall (and a recall of the same system), joined from NHTSA's recall file. State records list every make; make records add the model year by component table and each model's counts; national make records add each model by model year and the number of recall campaigns. A complaint is counted once however many parts it names. Only counts are kept: no narrative, VIN, city, name or complaint number.

resources.name: wage-enforcement
resources.title: Wage-and-hour and OSHA enforcement by county, state, act and industry (U.S. Department of Labor)
resources.description: What the U.S. Department of Labor found when it enforced wage and safety laws, counted for every county, state and territory and the US over the last ten complete federal fiscal years. From the Wage and Hour Division (WHD): concluded cases, cases with violations, back wages found owed, employees owed back wages, civil money penalties, Fair Labor Standards Act overtime and minimum wage back wages, and child labor violations. From the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), federal and state-plan offices: inspections (and how many followed a complaint, a referral, an accident or a fatality or catastrophe), violations cited (serious, willful, repeat), and penalties. State and US records add one record per law WHD enforces (FLSA, FMLA, Davis-Bacon, the Service Contract Act, H-2A, H-2B, H-1B, MSPA and others) and one per industry sector. Only counts and sums are published: no employer name, address or case number, and back wages are suppressed wherever 1 or 2 employees were owed.
